Article Title: Apple added these MacBooks to its ‘obsolete list’: What it means for users
Article Text:
How Apple's vintage and obsolete system works

What it means for users

A look back at what made these models notable

Apple has officially added the 2018 Retina MacBook Air, the 13‑inch 2018 MacBook Pro (four Thunderbolt 3 ports), and the 13‑inch 2017 MacBook Pro (two Thunderbolt 3 ports) to its obsolete products list. This means that the users of the above mentioned MacBook will not be able to receive hardware repairs. All three had previously been sitting on Apple's separate "vintage" list before being moved into the more restrictive obsolete category.Apple's classification system runs on a fixed timeline. A product is added to the vintage list once five years have passed since Apple last distributed it for sale, and it graduates to obsolete status at the seven-year mark. The distinction between the two categories matters significantly for owners: vintage products can still be repaired at Apple retail stores and Apple Authorized Service Providers as long as Apple has the necessary parts on hand. Obsolete devices, by contrast, are generally no longer eligible for repair at all, and Apple stops manufacturing replacement components for them going forward.Owners of these devices should be aware of the following:* No official repairs for obsolete products like the iPad mini 4.* Limited service for vintage products like the 2017 MacBook Air, depending on parts availability.* Software updates are unlikely, which may affect app compatibility and security.* Third-party repair options may be the only alternative for maintenance.The 2018 MacBook Air held a particular significance in the product line's history — it was the first Air model to include Touch ID and a Retina display, following earlier Air models that used a lower-resolution, less vibrant non-Retina screen. That same year also marked a broader redesign for the Air line, introducing smaller bezels and a thinner, lighter overall chassis.The 2017 MacBook Pro, meanwhile, ran on Intel's Kaby Lake processors and represented a fairly minor processor-focused update with few other significant changes. The following year's 2018 refresh added True Tone display support for the first time, along with a third-generation butterfly keyboard.
Article Summary: Apple has added the 2018 Retina MacBook Air, the 13‑inch 2018 MacBook Pro, and the 13-inch 2017 MacBook Pro to its obsolete products list. All three had previously been sitting on Apple's separate "vintage" list before being moved into the more restrictive obsolete category.

Article Title: FBI has a 'Public Service Announcement' for everyone on the internet: You may be targeted by ...
Article Text:
What is 'OAuth consent phishing', and what makes it dangerous

How 'OAuth Consent Phishing Works

The cyber division of Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has released a Public Service Announcement providing insight regarding a recent campaign of malicious cyber actors targeting prominent victims through a technique known as OAuth consent phishing. According to FBI advisory, "Since late 2025, malicious cyber actors have been targeting prominent victims, their family members, and personal acquaintances by directly messaging personal accounts with malicious links leveraging a technique known as 'OAuth consent phishing'.OAuth is a commonly used authorization framework which enables websites and Web applications to request access to a user's account on another application without the user exposing their login credentials to the requesting application.OAuth consent phishing is a deceptive, sophisticated approach to access user accounts without requiring a password. It typically begins with a phishing email or direct message through a CMA and, when the user clicks the malicious link, they are redirected to a legitimate communication provider permission request screen. If the user approves the request, they unwittingly grant high-level access to a malicious application controlled by the cyber actor.From that moment, the cyber actor can act on behalf of the user, including reading and sending emails, and accessing sensitive data without having access to the user's credentials. By registering malicious applications through legitimate authorization protocols and using social engineering tactics, cyber actors can bypass both passwords and multi-factor authentication, which makes consent phishing especially dangerous.FBI says that recently observed activity includes impersonating government officials, media, and other publicly known personalities on a commercial messaging application (CMA) and soliciting the targeted individual to access a malicious link under the guise of a file sharing service through an application under the malicious actor's control. Previous phishing campaigns have also impersonated event coordinators and planners, who sent malicious links to targets under the guise of an invitation to an event and the need to verify the target's identity through a malicious application under the actor's control.OAuth is a commonly used authorization framework which enables websites and Web applications to request access to a user's account on another application without the user exposing their login credentials to the requesting application.Historically, spear phishing efforts focused on social engineering ruses with links or access to malicious credential harvesting sites or malware deployment to gain access to target accounts or devices. OAuth consent phishing provides actors with persistent access to a target's account because once permission is obtained, it can only be revoked by the victim invalidating the token in their application security settings; not by changing the password.How internet users can protect themselvesMitigation strategies include increased scrutiny of communications from unfamiliar phone numbers, accounts, or that are not part of a known contact list. Additionally, independently verify the identity of the sender and only grant authorization to trusted applications.
Article Summary: Malicious cyber actors have been targeting prominent victims, their family members, and personal acquaintances by directly messaging personal accounts with malicious links. FBI says that recently observed activity includes impersonating government officials, media, and other publicly known personalities. OAuth consent phishing provides actors with persistent access to a target's account.

Article Title: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 models claimed to be ‘world’s most advanced models for coding and knowledge work’
Article Text:
Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 models

Claude Fable 5.1 brings lower costs and stronger coding performance: Anthropic

New Claude model aims to help with scientific research

Claude Mythos 5.1 is restricted to approved users

Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 availability

Anthropic has launched two new AI models, Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, with a focus on coding, research and complex knowledge work. The company says the new models can handle longer and harder tasks while also reducing costs for many users. Fable 5.1 is available to everyone, while Mythos 5.1 is limited to approved users working in areas such as cybersecurity and life sciences. The two models are essentially the same model, but come with different safety controls. Anthropic says Mythos 5.1 has more flexible safeguards for vetted researchers and security professionals. Announcing the two models, Anthropic said: “They’re the world’s most advanced models for coding and knowledge work—and their research capabilities offer an early glimpse of how AI models will contribute to scientific progress”.Anthropic says Claude Fable 5.1 will cost about 25% less than Fable 5 for typical workloads when usage is charged by tokens. For highly agentic tasks, which involve the AI working through many steps and using tools, the savings can reach about 45%.The lower cost comes mainly from a 75% cut in the price of cache reads. Cache reads allow the model to reuse information it has already processed. Anthropic says Fable 5.1 will continue to cost $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, while cache reads will cost $0.25 per million tokens.The company also says the model performed better than its predecessor on several tests. On CursorBench 3.2.0, for example, Fable 5.1 scored 73.4%, compared with 70.5% for Fable 5 and 70% for Opus 5.Anthropic is also highlighting the research abilities of its new models. In one test, Claude Fable 5.1 created a new high-resolution elevation map of part of Venus using old radar images from NASA's Magellan mission. Anthropic says the map shows details as small as two to three kilometres, compared with 10 to 20 kilometres in the earlier map.The company also tested Claude Mythos 5.1 for protein design. Anthropic says the model created protein binders that showed strong results in laboratory testing. Across 12 targets, the model achieved a hit rate of nearly 50%, which the company says is much higher than the typical 10% to 15% rate in protein design.Mythos 5.1 was also used to optimize seven open-source biology and genomics models. Anthropic says the models ran up to 2.5 times faster, while estimated GPU costs for some genome-wide analyses fell by 30% to 60%.Anthropic is not making Mythos 5.1 generally available. The model is being offered through trusted access programs for selected cybersecurity professionals and life sciences researchers. The company says these users can access capabilities that are restricted in the standard Fable 5.1 model.For cybersecurity, Anthropic says Fable 5.1 can now help find software vulnerabilities as part of defensive security work. However, tasks such as exploit generation and penetration testing remain restricted.The company also says its updated cybersecurity safeguards produce about 60% fewer false-positive interventions than the previous safeguards.For life sciences, Anthropic has created an access program for professionals using Mythos 5.1 for research and development. The program was developed in partnership with the US government.Anthropic is also introducing Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, or EFS, for enterprise customers. The system is designed to provide privacy similar to a zero-data-retention setup while allowing Anthropic to maintain safeguards against misuse. Under EFS, customer data is stored in cloud infrastructure controlled by the customer rather than Anthropic.The feature will begin rolling out to enterprise customers in phases later this fall.Claude Fable 5.1 is available immediately across Anthropic's platforms. Developers can also access it through the Claude API, while the model is available through cloud platforms including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure.Mythos 5.1, meanwhile, remains restricted to vetted users as Anthropic continues to balance its more advanced capabilities with safety concerns.
Article Summary: Claude Fable 5.1 will cost about 25% less for typical workloads when usage is charged by tokens. For highly agentic tasks, which involve the AI working through many steps and using tools, the savings can reach about 45%. The lower cost comes mainly from a 75% cut in the price of cache reads.

Article Title: Sam Altman admits AI models 'scare' him and he understands why world is anxious; but wants everyone to take responsibility
Article Text:
OpenAI CEO Sam ​Altman

Sam Altman admits tension between excitement surrounding AI capabilites

Here’s the full post shared by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has admitted that the rapid rise of AI can be “scary” adding he understands why people around the world are anxious about increasingly powerful AI models. Sharing a post on X (formerly Twitter), Sam Altman said that the company itself has been living with the tension between excitement and fear as AI capabilities improve. But Altman also believes that simply worrying about AI is not enough. He wants society, AI companies and others to take what is happening seriously and evolve alongside the technology, while making safety and alignment a top priority.“We have been living with the tension between being excited and anxious about progress for some time, and it is still discordant for us,” Altman said adding “We know it is much more discordant for other people. And yet, we believe strongly that the world needs to understand where AI is going and how models perform in the real world. More importantly, we believe the world will need aligned AI to manage the future phases of this transition”.In the post, Sam Altman said that there is a clear tension between the excitement surrounding increasingly capable AI and the need to move carefully.“There is an obvious tension here: on one hand, Astra is very good and we are excited to see what people will build with it.We are proud of our work.”But he added that OpenAI believes caution is necessary at this stage of AI development.“On the other hand, we are clearly in a phase of development where we believe caution is warranted, and we are pacing our progress to ensure that we can meet the safety standards required by new capability levels.”"Over the summer, we have been sprinting on safety priorities; it's more important than ever for capabilities and safeguards to advance together. We have more to do but have made a lot of progress. We are also going to be launching our next model soon.There is an obvious tension here: on one hand, Astra is very good and we are excited to see what people will build with it. We are proud of our work.On the other hand, we are clearly in a phase of development where we believe caution is warranted, and we are pacing our progress to ensure that we can meet the safety standards required by new capability levels.Astra has been done training for a while now and is a significant step forward in both capabilities and alignment. For the models after that, we have been slowing things as needed to ensure that we can do sufficient work on safety and alignment.AI is getting extremely capable; no one fully understands the consequences of this. Managing the transition to a world with abundant and powerful AI to optimize for safety and benefits to people should be one of the highest priorities in the world. It is our highest priority at OpenAI.We have been living with the tension between being excited and anxious about progress for some time, and it is still discordant for us. We know it is much more discordant for other people. And yet, we believe strongly that the world needs to understand where AI is going and how models perform in the real world. More importantly, we believe the world will need aligned AI to manage the future phases of this transition.An iterative loop where society and this technology evolve together is what will lead to the highest chance of getting this right.So we hope you enjoy our new model, and we hope the world continues to take what’s happening in AI extremely seriously."
Article Summary: ChatGPT-maker OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has admitted that the rapid rise of AI can be “scary” adding he understands why people around the world are anxious about increasingly powerful AI models. He wants society, AI companies and others to take what is happening seriously and evolve alongside the technology.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness.

Article Title: Kolhapur civic body to carry out patchwork filling using state-of-the-art technology
Article Text:
The Municipal Corporation is piloting the modern ‘Insta Road Patcher’ technology to fill potholes on city roads quickly and durably. A demonstration of this machine, which utilizes GIPSAT bitumen technology, was conducted on the main road between Papachi Tikti and Pan Lane on Monday noon.

Kolhapur:





The Kolhapur municipal corporation is piloting the modern ‘Insta Road Patcher’ technology to fill potholes on city roads quickly and durably. A demonstration of this machine, which utilizes GIPSAT bitumen technology, was conducted on the main road between Papachi Tikti and Pan Lane on Monday noon.The ‘Insta Road Patcher’ tech employs pressure-sensitive material, enabling potholes to be filled within minutes, eliminating the need for heavy machinery such as trucks, dumpers, or large road rollers, and allows road repair work to be carried out with minimal manpower.KMC Commissioner, Dr Rajendra Bharud, MLA Rajesh Kshirsagar, who is the head of state planning commission, and Vishal Shirale, the chairperson of the standing committee, visited the site to inspect the demonstration.This technology utilises a ready-made mixture of bitumen, crushed stone (aggregate), and special chemicals, which does not require heating, and is suitable for use across all seasons and weather conditions. There is no need to wait for the surface to cool down, since the road can be opened to traffic immediately after the repair.Patching a single pothole takes approximately ten minutes. As the repairs made using this technology are capable of lasting at least two years, it can help reduce the costs associated with frequent road repairs, proving useful for small roads and urgent pothole repairs.Filling potholes using traditional methods requires significant manpower, time, and machinery, with the problem of potholes reappearing shortly after repair. Against this backdrop, the IRP-GIPSAT technology could serve as a faster, and more efficient alternative for road repair work.KMC commissioner Dr Rajendra Bharud said, “There are about 1100km of roads in Kolhapur city. Of these, more than 200km are filled every year by the municipal corporation. The concerned company has taken a guarantee of two years for their potholes and if potholes reoccur, then they themselves will repair the road.”
Article Summary: The ‘Insta Road Patcher’ tech employs pressure-sensitive material, enabling potholes to be filled within minutes. It eliminates the need for heavy machinery such as trucks, dumpers, or large road rollers, and allows road repair work to be carried out with minimal manpower.

Article Title: Fraudster uses Raigad SP’s WhatsApp display photo to dupe police staff, seeks Rs 50,000
Article Text:
A cyber fraudster impersonated Raigad SP on WhatsApp, targeting police personnel for money transfers, but the scam attempt was foiled. (AI-generated image)





NAVI MUMBAI: Raigad Cyber Police have registered a case against an unidentified fraudster who allegedly used the WhatsApp Display Picture (DP) of Raigad Superintendent of Police (SP) Anchal Dalal to deceive several police personnel into transferring money.On Thursday, the fraudster sent a message to Raigad SP's reader, PSI Siddheshwar Murkute, asking him to transfer money urgently. Murkute immediately realised that it was a modus operandi commonly used by cyber scammers, as the WhatsApp message was sent from an international number that was not saved in his mobile phone.Thereafter, PSI Murkute learnt that the same scammer had sent similar messages to several Raigad police personnel. Fortunately, no one fell prey to the fraud, as the police personnel were aware of this modus operandi used by cyber fraudsters.Subsequently, PSI Murkute registered an FIR against the unidentified accused under the relevant section of the BNS for the offence of cheating by personation.The complainant, PSI Murkute, said, "I had received the WhatsApp message from an international number and the DP was of Raigad SP Anchal Dalal.The message read, 'I am in a meeting and my mobile is switched off. Immediately transfer Rs 50,000 to my bank account.' I knew the message sender was a scammer. I deliberately replied asking for the bank account number by pretending to send the money. As I received the bank account number from the scammer, it will be useful for the cyber police team to trace the bank account holder. "PSI Murkute added, "One police officer had received a WhatsApp message from the same international number asking to transfer Rs 2,000 by impersonating SP madam and claiming that it was required for filling diesel in the car, and that her mobile battery had drained and she was unable to pay online at the fuel station."API Amol Jadhav of Raigad Cyber Police said, "The cyber scammers use VPNs (Virtual Private Networks) to mask their identity. However, the Internet Protocol (IP) address of the WhatsApp number used by the accused will be obtained to trace the location, and the accused will soon be behind bars."
Article Summary: A cyber fraudster impersonated Raigad SP on WhatsApp, targeting police personnel for money transfers. Fortunately, no one fell prey to the fraud, as the police personnel were aware of this modus operandi used by cyber fraudsters. One police officer received a WhatsApp message from the same international number asking to transfer Rs 2,000 by impersonating SP madam.

Article Title: Madurai ward 80 residents can get rewards for segregating waste
Article Text:
Under the Solid Waste Management Rules 2026, Mayor in charge (Deputy Mayor) T Nagarajan and Corporation Commissioner Gaurav Kumar, inaugurated a source segregation rewards initiative covering 3,500 households in Jaihindpuram in Madurai on Tuesday.





Madurai: As the Solid Waste Management Rules 2026 come into effect across Madurai, to encourage residents to participate in source segregation practices, mayor in charge (deputy mayor) T Nagarajan and corporation commissioner Gaurav Kumar inaugurated a reward initiative covering 3,500 households in ward 80 of Jaihindpuram.The rewards programme, under the initiative “My waste, my responsibility,” will monitor source segregation compliance for a month, tracking houses following best practices on a publicly available website. The civic body partnered with academia to introduce a tech-driven evaluation framework.Following the inauguration, senior corporation officials flagged off a newly assigned fleet of municipal collection vehicles dedicated to gathering segregated waste from the ward. “Waste collection vehicles have been equipped with different bins to prevent waste mixing, and workers have been instructed not to accept mixed waste. Regular inspections of source segregation will continue across the city, and fines will be imposed on repeat violations,” the official said.Households that consistently segregate their waste every day for a full month earn daily points that qualify them for prizes.
Article Summary: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules 2026, Mayor in charge (Deputy Mayor) T Nagarajan and Corporation Commissioner Gaurav Kumar, inaugurated a source segregation rewards initiative. The rewards programme will monitor source segregation compliance for a month, tracking houses following best practices on a publicly available website.

Article Title: Deputy mayor announces incentives for segregating waste
Article Text: Madurai: While Madurai corporation is making source segregation mandatory across all 100 wards, mayor in charge (deputy mayor) T Nagarajan has announced incentives for the households that follow best practices and properly segregate waste for a month in his ward 80.Covering 3,500 households, the drive aims to encourage residents to segregate their daily waste before handing it over to door-to-door collection. Corporation officials, along with NGO Olirum Madurai, distributed four waste bins in different colours to every participating household in the ward.To monitor compliance and digitise the process, a team of students and faculty members, led by dean Shivaranjani, from Sethu Institute of Technology has deployed a tracking system via a mobile app and web portal. The team is fixing QR code stickers on the doors of 3,500 houses. Every morning, sanitation workers will scan the QR codes as they collect the segregated waste, enabling the system to evaluate household compliance and assign daily performance scores based on how well the waste has been segregated.Nagarajan said the incentive will increase awareness and foster cleanliness in the locality.
Article Summary: Madurai corporation is making source segregation mandatory across all 100 wards. Mayor in charge T Nagarajan has announced incentives for households that follow best practices and properly segregate waste for a month in his ward 80. Covering 3,500 households, the drive aims to encourage residents to segregate their daily waste before handing it over to door-to-door collection.

Article Title: ANPR camera system launched in Namakkal district to curb traffic violations
Article Text: NAMAKKAL: An automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) camera system was launched in Namakkal district on Monday to impose fines on traffic violators. The facility was inaugurated at the Namakkal–Salem Road corner junction by district superintendent of police Yadav Krish Ashok.The ANPR system will automatically detect violations such as using mobile phones while driving, riding w-wheelers without helmets and driving without seat belts. Fines will be issued digitally. The penalty amount and receipt will be sent directly to the violator’s registered mobile number.Speaking to reporters, S P Yadav Krish Ashok said, “Road accidents have claimed 348 lives in Namakkal district in the past eight months. Strict monitoring is essential to reduce fatalities. The ANPR camera system will help enforce discipline among motorists. Riders must wear helmets for their own safety and that of their families. Those indulging in reckless stunts will also be closely monitored and penalised.”
Article Summary: The facility was inaugurated at the Namakkal–Salem Road corner junction by district superintendent of police Yadav Krish Ashok. The ANPR system will automatically detect violations such as using mobile phones while driving, riding w-wheelers without helmets and driving without seat belts.

Article Title: In 2015, Florida scientists poured 5 gallons of red dye into Silver River to study how water moved as its clear waters were turning algae-green; they found it took roughly 11.5 hours to travel 5.1 mil
Article Text:
Representation of a dye tracer spreading through a clear spring-fed river, illustrating how scientists can visualise the movement and mixing of water. Image Credits: ChatGPT.

A dye turns invisible movement into a measurable signal

What the tracer revealed about the river

Silver River gorge, near Cadamstown, Co. Offaly. Image Credits: Wikimedia Commons.

Following the river to understand its changing ecology

In 2015, researchers used a fluorescent dye to trace the movement of water through the Silver River, one of Florida’s major spring-fed waterways. The experiment was designed to measure how quickly water travelled through the river, how it mixed along the way and how long it remained in different sections.According to the University of Florida’s Center for Wetlands and Stream Ecosystem Research , the 2015 dye-tracing experiment was part of a broader research effort examining changes in Florida’s spring ecosystems. These included a shift from clear-water conditions dominated by submerged aquatic vegetation towards greater algal growth. Researchers were investigating how changes in river hydraulics and nutrient movement might be related to these ecological changes.On March 8, 2015, researchers from the University of Florida’s Watershed Ecology Lab released five gallons of Rhodamine ET, a red fluorescent dye, at the Main Spring vent in the Silver River. They tracked the dye downstream using nine monitoring stations, including three in-stream fluorometers and six automated samplers. More than 20 student volunteers also collected 318 additional samples overnight. These measurements allowed researchers to calculate the river’s velocity and residence time, referring to how long water remained within the monitored system and its different sections.Fluorescent dye tracing is commonly used to study the movement and mixing of water because the tracer can be detected at successive points along a river.In the Silver River, the method allowed researchers to follow the same water signal downstream rather than relying only on measurements taken at individual locations. The 2015 results showed that the dye travelled the roughly 5.1-mile monitored reach in about 11.5 hours, according to the project’s reported results. That works out to an average travel rate of about 0.44 miles per hour, although the dye did not move at the same rate throughout the river.Researchers later compared the 2015 results with those from another Silver River tracer experiment carried out in 2009. A University of Florida Water Institute study found that the river’s hydraulic behaviour changed under different discharge conditions. At higher discharge, the mean residence time of the spring run decreased, while transient storage increased. In practical terms, this means that changes in river flow can affect both how quickly water travels downstream and how much water temporarily exchanges with slower-moving areas along the channel. Such changes can, in turn, influence how nutrients and other substances move through the river.The researchers were also examining whether these hydraulic conditions were related to differences in algal biomass. Initial findings from the University of Florida showed a negative correlation between water velocity and algal cover in benthic and periphytic habitats. The tracer experiments therefore provided a way to examine the physical conditions alongside the biological observations. Where water moves faster, organisms experience different flow conditions than in areas where water remains longer. These differences can affect the transport and retention of nutrients and other substances, helping researchers examine how changes in river flow may be associated with changes in the river’s biological communities.The Silver River experiment formed part of a larger three-year interdisciplinary research project funded by the St Johns River Water Management District. Ten University of Florida researchers from four departments contributed to the programme, which examined the causes of ecological change in Florida’s springs and possible responses. The tracer experiment focused on how water moved through the Silver River, providing measurements that helped researchers understand the physical conditions within the spring system.The tracer data were also used to calibrate and validate a model of water movement and dye transport through the river. By tracking the tracer from the spring vent downstream, researchers were able to measure how quickly it travelled through different sections of the river and compare those observations with the model's predictions. This provided a more detailed picture of water movement through the system and helped place the biological changes observed in the river within their underlying hydrological conditions.
Article Summary: Researchers used a fluorescent dye to trace the movement of water through the Silver River, one of Florida’s major spring-fed waterways. The experiment was designed to measure how quickly water travelled through the river, how it mixed along the way and how long it remained in different sections. Researchers were investigating how changes in river hydraulics and nutrient movement might be related to these ecological changes.

Article Title: '1 tick, 2 ticks': Kin seek hope in text-delivery reports in Nepal
Article Text:
A change in message-delivery status or a last tower ping became a potential clue to where a missing relative might be

TRISHULI BAZAAR (NUWAKOT, NEPAL): For two days after Serbian citizen Enisa Lekovic disappeared in the floods in Nepal, a WhatsApp message sent by her daughter sat on a single grey tick - sent, but not delivered. Then, on Aug 28, the screen changed: the tick had turned into two blue ones - the family's first real sign of hope. On Tuesday, that hope turned into relief when her daughter, Ines Todorovic, confirmed that Lekovic had been found alive and was on her way to Kathmandu. "I can't describe what I felt these days," she wrote on social media.Like Lekovic's family, relatives of hydropower workers missing in the Bhote Koshi-Trishuli flood began turning phones into search evidence after rescue teams could not provide definite answers. They repeatedly sent messages, watching whether single grey ticks turned into two, while many bypassed conventional search desks and approached Nepal Police Cyber Bureau, Nepal Telecom, Ncell and rescue teams with mobile numbers, asking them to trace the last tower and sector where the phones had been active before signals disappeared.For families with little else to go on, a change in message-delivery status or a last tower ping became a potential clue to where a missing relative might be - and where rescuers should look next.Relatives of Roshan Kumar Joshi, an environmental expert from Morang working at the 216MW Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project, repeatedly messaged him after he went out of contact. "Roshan, are you safe? Please reply as soon as you find any connectivity," read one. The single tick did not change as relatives searched social media, contacted project staff and waited for news. At the Upper Trishuli-3B Hydropower Project, relatives of engineer Pramila Pathak, 32, wrote: "Pramila, are rescue teams near your quarters? Send a location pin if your phone turns on. " That message too remained undelivered.Telecom officials, however, said that a single grey tick could not show whether someone was alive, trapped or even carrying a functioning phone. Nepal Telecom said that after power supplies failed in affected areas, it shut down data and other services and kept only 2G voice services running to conserve battery backup. Internet-based messaging platforms such as WhatsApp could not deliver messages.Private mobile operator Ncell also issued a statement cautioning against drawing conclusions from a phone going offline. "A phone can disappear from the network because it was damaged by water or because its battery ran out. Disconnection does not necessarily mean the person was caught in the disaster. They may have reached safety and simply run out of battery."Meanwhile, the last mobile tower and sector used by a handset offered a more specific geographical clue. Families approached the Nepal Police Cyber Bureau, Nepal Telecom, Ncell and rescue teams with mobile numbers and requests to establish where missing workers' phones had last connected before signals disappeared. Joshi's family eventually received one such record: "Ramche-C, 9.10am, Aug 26." It showed that his handset had last connected through sector C of the Ramche tower in Rasuwa, allowing relatives to narrow the direction in which they wanted rescuers to search. Chitragupta Bhatta, who worked at Trishuli Hydropower Company Limited, left another significant digital trace. His family received: "Neupane Chaur, 9.26am, Aug 26." His phone remained active more than 15 minutes after the flood struck the area, raising hopes that he might have reached or remained inside a tunnel. "...We began to hope that perhaps he is inside a tunnel," a relative said. "So many days have passed... It is becoming difficult to hold on."A senior executive with Huawei Nepal said mobile towers generally divided coverage into three directional sectors. "By mapping the direction, we can determine whether the phone was on the river side or the mountain side."Privacy rules created another hurdle. Families could move beyond physical search desks in their hunt for clues, but telecom operators could not directly hand them subscriber's location records. A Nepal Telecom said such information is shared with security agencies through authorised channels.
Article Summary: Families of hydropower workers missing in the Bhote Koshi-Trishuli flood began turning phones into search evidence. They repeatedly sent messages, watching whether single grey ticks turned into two. Many bypassed conventional search desks and approached Nepal Police Cyber Bureau, Nepal Telecom, Ncell and rescue teams with mobile numbers.

Article Title: ChatGPT is first AI chatbot to face tougher EU rules
Article Text:
ChatGPT is first AI chatbot to face tougher EU rules﻿

ChatGPT will have to comply with tougher safety rules after the EU added it Monday to a list of digital services subject to greater legal scrutiny, a first for an AI chatbot.Brussels also designated Reddit and Roblox as “very large” online platforms, a label that comes with additional obligations and oversight. “ChatGPT, Reddit and Roblox will now be held to a higher standard of scrutiny and accountability in the EU, in line with their large impact on our citizens and society,” EU technology chief Henna Virkkunen said.The designation applies to platforms and search engines with over 45 million monthly active users in the 27-nation bloc, a threshold the three platforms reported meeting, the commission said. The three now have four months to comply with additional obligations under the Digital Services Act, a content law the EU has deployed to rein in Big Tech.

Article Title: Australia planted eucalyptus trees to fight rising soil salinity; decades later scientists found the plantations were changing groundwater but not the soil nature
Article Text:
Eucalyptus cladocalyx ‘nana’. Image Credit: ERA Nurseries

How did eucalyptus plantations change groundwater and soil salinity in Australia

The groundwater changed, but the saline seep remained

Why didn't the eucalyptus trees solve the salinity problem

Image Credit: AI generated

Some eucalyptus species performed better over 15 years

nana

A long-term lesson from Australia's eucalyptus plantations

Australia planted eucalyptus trees to fight rising soil salinity, hoping that thirsty, deep-rooted vegetation could help control the groundwater processes behind the problem. A long-running experiment in south-western Australia later showed that the effects of such plantations were more complicated than simply planting trees and waiting for the land to recover. Researchers established a mixed eucalyptus plantation above a saline seep in 1976 and monitored how the trees affected groundwater levels and salt movement for 15 years. The study found clear signs that the plantation used more water than nearby crops and pasture, while groundwater conditions also changed over time. Yet the trees did not stop the saline seep as researchers had hoped. Published in ‘ Agricultural Water Management ,’ the research offers a revealing look at why tree planting can influence groundwater and salinity without necessarily solving the underlying problem everywhere it is tried.The study examined a plantation established on about 12% of a small farm catchment. The trees were planted above a saline seep, an area where salty groundwater had reached or approached the surface and damaged the land. The researchers wanted to identify eucalyptus species that could use large amounts of water and potentially help reclaim such affected areas. According to the study, the catchment contained two important groundwater systems.One was a deep aquifer in the lower part of the landscape and the other, a shallower seasonal aquifer. The researchers monitored changes in groundwater level and salinity using piezometers, allowing them to follow how conditions changed as the plantation developed.The results showed that the plantation was having a noticeable effect on water use. Changes in groundwater levels, along with observations of perched water, indicated that the trees were using more water than the nearby crop and pasture vegetation. This was an important finding because the basic idea behind planting trees in salt-affected agricultural landscapes was that trees could alter the movement of water through the soil. If less water moved downwards into the groundwater system, or if trees removed more water from the landscape, they could potentially help limit the processes that bring salt towards the surface.The researchers found that the plantation influenced groundwater chemistry as well as water levels. Chloride concentrations in the deep aquifer fell by approximately 20% between 1977 and 1984. The decline was greater at the middle of the slope than further downslope. This suggested that conditions beneath the catchment were changing, although the changes were not uniform across the landscape. At the same time, the study found larger stores of salt in the soil downslope than at the middle of the slope. There was also visual evidence that salt continued to be discharged extensively through the saline seep throughout the experiment. In other words, the trees were clearly affecting the local water system, but their presence did not bring the expected recovery of the seep. The research showed why this distinction matters. A plantation may increase water use and change groundwater conditions without having enough influence over the particular underground system responsible for a saline area.One of the most important findings of the study concerned the location of the plantation. The researchers identified the site's underground geology as a significant reason why the trees failed to control the seepage. The plantation was located in an area where the relevant aquifer appeared to be ‘confined.’ That meant the groundwater system beneath the site was not easy for the trees to influence in the way researchers had hoped. This finding highlighted a practical limitation of tree-based approaches to salinity. Planting species that use substantial amounts of water may not be enough on its own. The location of groundwater, the way water moves through underground layers and the position of the plantation within the wider landscape can all affect the outcome. The study therefore showed that managing salinity is not simply a question of selecting the thirstiest trees. Understanding the underground environment is equally important.The experiment also compared the performance of different eucalyptus species. The original aim was to rank species partly according to water use, which the researchers assessed through factors including leaf area and survival. Tree growth was rapid during the early years of the experiment, continuing strongly until 1981. After that, growth declined. 15 years later, four species emerged as the most promising among those tested. These included ‘Eucalyptus cladocalyx var.,’ ‘Eucalyptus cladocalyx,’ ‘Eucalyptus occidentalis’ and ‘Eucalyptus sargentii.’ Their performance did not mean that the plantation had solved the saline seep problem. Instead, it showed that some species were better suited than others to the demanding conditions of the site. A tree can survive well and use considerable amounts of water while still being unable to alter a groundwater system enough to stop salt from reaching the surface.The 15-year experiment provided a more realistic picture of what tree planting could not achieve in salt-affected farmland. The eucalyptus plantation used more water than the surrounding vegetation, and conditions in the deep groundwater system also shifted, including a significant fall in chloride concentration. Yet the saline seep continued to discharge salt. As per the study, this outcome was due to the underground conditions beneath the plantation. The research pointed towards a broader lesson that the success of planting trees depends not only on the trees, but also on the landscape in which they are planted. For areas struggling with rising groundwater and soil salinity, the findings suggest that planting eucalyptus can be a useful tool, but it is not a solution. Trees can change groundwater behaviour, without necessarily controlling the source of the problem. Only by monitoring the plantation for many years were researchers able to see both the benefits of greater tree water use and the limits imposed by the site's hidden groundwater system.
Article Summary: Australia planted eucalyptus trees to fight rising soil salinity. Researchers monitored how the trees affected groundwater levels and salt movement for 15 years. The study found clear signs that the plantation used more water than nearby crops and pasture, while groundwater conditions also changed over time. Yet the trees did not stop the saline seep as researchers had hoped.

Article Title: Scotland quarry expansion uncovered a 2,000-year-old woman’s grave; archaeologists were stunned by its carefully built stone walls
Article Text:
'Beautifully made' Iron Age burial site containing the skeleton of a woman at a quarry in Sutherland. Image Credit: Highland Archaeological Services (HAS)

Discovery of the 2,000-year-old unique burial in Scotland

What did the Iron Age grave of a woman look like

Further analysis is being carried out on the grave. Image Credit: Highland Archaeological Services (HAS)

Absence of objects in the women’s grave

What can the skeleton reveal about the woman

A nearly 2,000-year-old carefully constructed stone-lined burial containing the remains of a woman has been discovered at a quarry in Sutherland, Scotland, revealing an unexpected glimpse of life and death at that time. Archaeologists from Highland Archaeological Services(HAS) discovered Evelix, near Dornoch, while carrying out work ahead of a planned quarry expansion. The grave was found within an area where evidence of ancient settlement has also been identified, including features that may once have supported timber roundhouses. What caught the archaeologists’ attention was the unusual quality of the stonework. The structure was so neatly built that, at first, the team wondered whether it could have been modern. Instead, the construction style and archaeological evidence pointed towards the Iron Age, with the woman apparently having remained undisturbed for centuries beneath the ground.The discovery was made during archaeological work connected with the planned expansion of the Evelix quarry near Dornoch. According to the BBC, HAS was working for local quarry firm ‘GF Job’ when archaeologists encountered the stone-lined structure.The location was already considered archaeologically important. The Highland Historic Environment Record shows that the wider Evelix area has produced evidence of prehistoric activity, including burial remains, cremation burials, pottery and features linked to earlier settlement. This newly discovered structure stood out because of its carefully constructed stone lining. Instead of looking like a simple hole dug into the ground, it had been deliberately built with substantial masonry. As per the BBC, archaeologist Lynne McKeggie said the team initially thought the structure might be modern because of how well the stonework had been put together. That first impression quickly changed once the remains and other evidence were examined.The structure was dug into sand and measured approximately 3 metres long, 2 metres wide and 1 metre deep, according to the BBC. A small stone staircase formed part of the construction, adding another feature to the burial. Inside, the remains of an individual were found tucked into one corner. The archaeological team believes the individual was a woman and that she may have lain there undisturbed since the Iron Age. The careful construction is one of the most striking parts of the discovery. The stonework had been fitted together so neatly that the archaeologists described the structure as ‘beautifully made.’ Its appearance raises questions about why so much effort was put into creating it.The Highland Historic Environment Record provides an important background to the discovery. The people who built the structure were working without modern machinery, yet they created a substantial stone-lined space with a staircase. The result survived beneath the landscape for roughly two millennia before quarry-related archaeological work exposed it. Earlier archaeological work at the Evelix quarry area had already shown that the landscape contained evidence of prehistoric activity.The burial does not appear to have contained a collection of obvious grave goods. The BBC reported that no objects were found inside the structure, although archaeologists did identify a large quantity of animal bone. The absence of objects does not make the discovery less significant. In fact, it leaves more questions about the purpose of the structure and the circumstances surrounding the woman's burial. The animal remains may provide useful evidence as further analysis takes place. The construction itself can offer clues about the importance of the site to the people who used it. The wider archaeological record for Evelix also shows that prehistoric burials and settlement activity had previously occurred in the area.The remains could eventually provide a much more personal picture of the woman who was buried at the site. BBC reports that GF Job is funding further analysis of the human remains. Specialists will study the skeleton in greater detail, with the aim of learning more about the individual and the circumstances surrounding the burial. For now, many details remain unknown. Her exact age, background and life story cannot be established simply from the discovery itself. Those answers will depend on the scientific examination still to come. Archaeologists are using photographs and 3D scans to preserve information about the structure and the position of the remains.Once the further analysis has been carried out, the skeleton will be made available to Treasure Trove Scotland for potential allocation to a museum. What began as archaeological work ahead of a modern quarry expansion has revealed a carefully constructed resting place that had remained hidden for around 2,000 years. The woman's identity may never be known, but the grave itself has survived as a quiet reminder of the care and effort that people in Iron Age Sutherland could invest in remembering their dead.
Article Summary: Archaeologists from Highland Archaeological Services(HAS) discovered Evelix, near Dornoch, while carrying out work ahead of a planned quarry expansion. The structure was dug into sand and measured approximately 3 metres long, 2 metres wide and 1 metre deep. Inside, the remains of an individual were found tucked into one corner. Archaeologists believe the individual was a woman and that she may have lain there undisturbed since the Iron Age.

Article Title: In 2024, England turned old fishing nets into a 16-metre footbridge; the 3.5-tonne structure needs smaller foundations and less maintenance than a conventional bridge
Article Text:
The project used modular blocks, which mostly can be placed by hand, instead of traditional reinforced-concrete retaining walls. The blocks fit together like a Lego system, with little or no mortar needed.

Lego-like construction system

A journey by land and sea

Lower carbon footprint, less maintenance

Old fishing nets seldom find a second life. But in Kent, England, the nets are being turned into something much more ambitious. The used nets have been transformed to make a 16-metre-long footbridge to carry people over a marina entrance with minimal environmental impact during construction. Media reports from 2024 say that the Environment Agency built an innovative bridge at Twyford Marina in Yalding using recycled materials, lightweight engineering, and a construction method to reduce the amount of concrete used. The 16-metre bridge is part of the Medway Valley Walk and offers pedestrians a new route across the entrance to Twyford Marina. It also makes it easier for boats to enter and leave the marina. The bridge deck and main structure are made of fibre-reinforced polymer, or FRP, from recycled old fishing nets. The material is a blend of strength and light weight and is particularly useful in a challenging construction location. According to reports, the completed bridge is much lighter at 3.5 tons than many traditional structures of a similar size. The weight reduction also allowed engineers to use smaller support foundations.The innovation is not only the bridge itself. If we go by the GOV UK website, the project used modular blocks, which mostly can be placed by hand, instead of traditional reinforced-concrete retaining walls. The blocks fit together like a Lego system, with little or no mortar needed. According to experts, this method requires less reinforced concrete, making construction simpler and potentially reducing the project's carbon footprint. Lighter materials and smaller footings also allowed the bridge to be constructed in a site where it would have been difficult to deliver large construction equipment.The bridge's journey to Kent was no less strange. According to the GOV UK website, the deck was built in the Netherlands before being shipped to Nottinghamshire and fitted with handrails. From there, the 3.5-ton structure was transported by road to Yalding. Her last voyage was by barge up the River Medway. When the bridge reached the marina, a crane set it in place. The project has given a new lease of life to discarded fishing nets, giving them a useful second life in a structure designed to serve walkers and boat users for years. Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.

Article Title: Tata Elxsi, Sarla Aviation to develop air taxi; first test flight targeted in 2 years
Article Text:
Tata Elxsi has expertise in aerospace, software and flight-critical digital engineering to support the aircraft's development, testing and certification.

NEW DELHI: Tata Elxsi, India’s leading design and technology services firm, will work with air mobility company Sarla Aviation to develop of “Shunya”, the latter’s six-seater plus one pilot electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft. Shunya’s first flight is targeted within the next 18 to 24 months, with certification activities expected to follow for the eVTOL that is being designed for a range of over 300 km with vertical take-off and landing capability with fixed-wing cruise.Tata Elxsi has expertise in aerospace, software and flight-critical digital engineering to support the aircraft's development, testing and certification. Under the collaboration, Tata Elxsi will provide engineering support across avionics such as flight control systems, software integration, testing, verification and validation, and certification, while Sarla Aviation will lead the design, development and type certification of the Shunya platform. The engagement also creates opportunities to extend support across sensor fusion-based navigation software, industrial and structural design, and airworthiness test support.Sarla Aviation co-founder and CEO Adrian Schmidt said: “Building a new class of aircraft is not simply an engineering challenge. It requires bringing together people and organisations willing to solve problems that have never been solved before in this market.Tata Elxsi's experience in complex aerospace systems gives us access to capabilities that are critical as we take Shunya from concept to reality. What excites me most about this collaboration is that it brings together two teams that believe advanced air mobility can move from ambition to everyday infrastructure much sooner than many think. ”Tata Elxsi CEO and MD Manoj Raghavan said: “Every major shift in transportation has been enabled by a combination of engineering innovation and ecosystem readiness. Advanced air mobility is no different, and Sarla Aviation's vision for Shunya reflects the ambition driving this transformation. Initiatives like this create opportunities to apply expertise built across aerospace, mobility and digital technologies to entirely new aviation platforms. ”Jayaraj Rajapandian, Tata Elxsi head of aerospace, added: “Shunya is a reminder of how quickly aerospace innovation is evolving in shaping the Technology landscape in India. As aircraft become increasingly fly-by-wire, electrified and connected, entirely new opportunities are emerging to rethink how people, goods and critical services move. We are excited to work alongside Sarla Aviation as they take this vision forward and contribute to the next phase of its journey. ”Beyond Shunya, the partnership is expected to help strengthen capabilities relevant to logistics, air ambulance services and defence-related applications. Tata Elxsi says advanced air mobility is a natural extension of the connected, autonomous and electrification transformation reshaping transportation. By bringing together expertise from aerospace and mobility, Tata Elxsi aims to help build the foundations for advanced air mobility platforms in the country.
